source.review_note: Root independently approved the lower/top-end cutpoints, matched timing-component handoff, oil/filter closure, cold-start and post-repair commissioning. Exact OEM PDF40 crank/gear break-in reviewed visually. Protective-cloth accounting and scope copy corrections applied. Physical validation remains separate.

title: Major engine rebuild and bike reassembly
completeness: Assembled-bike major engine walkthrough with measured top end, retained sound cases, case bearings, complete crank assembly, gearbox, oil pump and clutch drives, refit and crank/gear/top-end break-in. Retained water pump, pressure-relief, starter and electrical internals and pressed connecting-rod rebuilding remain excluded. External actual-work checks and physical validation gaps remain visible.

applicability.included: Exact stock US 2025 YZ450F with serviceable frame, engine mounting interfaces, intact chain/sprockets and operating brakes. Cable clutch. No automatic year inheritance.
excluded: Head resurfacing, cylinder rebore/replate, aftermarket parts or ring filing
Water-pump, starter-motor, pressure-relief valve and stator electrical internal rebuilding

prerequisites: Match exact stock installed engine and cable-clutch interfaces; preserve original hose/cable routing photographs.
Independent engine, swingarm and chassis support required while the shared pivot is withdrawn. Wheels, suspension and brake hydraulic circuits remain assembled.
Serviceable intact stock chain, sprockets and working rear brake are required for the attributed manual sprocket-nut holding technique; no impact, heat or case jamming.

The completed lower-engine and top-end bench work must return a sealed engine with all plugs/covers/filter/O-rings correctly fitted and documented timing, clearance, lubrication and free-rotation checks before refit.
Read the scope and arrange refit/commissioning before teardown.
Have exact diagrams available for head/cam order, timing, guide height and ring-gap orientation.
For guide renewal, arrange actual specialist seat refacing and separate new lapping/running valves.
Confirm measuring tools, new seals/gaskets and specified lubricants are available.
Have original illustrated manual and torque-check sheet available.
Arrange qualified assessment for required inaccessible checks or checks outside operator capability.
Do not record work as completed unless physically performed.

The head-gasket pressure test is performed within this route using the reviewed Mityvac method and verified actual adapter fit. First oil-flow startup follows cold tester attachment; no prior post-repair startup is assumed.
Plan actual qualified tank cleaning, seat refacing if chosen and inaccessible repaired-part/joint checks before teardown; these cannot be completed by a booking or a passed app check.
Have the cited gear-stack, case-bearing, fastener-length, timing and clutch-spring diagrams available.
Resolve suspected failures in excluded retained assemblies before teardown.
Have correct stock replacement parts, new seals/gaskets/circlips/staked nut/lock washer and calibrated tools.
Plan actual stock crank/chain/cam replacement as the matched set required by lower-chain inspection; lower-drive work must not leave incompatible retained cams for the later top-end checks.

steps.title: Record the engine and job condition
steps.instruction: Record the exact stock engine identity, running condition and reason for removal. Photograph hose, electrical and bracket routing before access. Prepare an independently supported engine bench and a controlled lift with a helper; this guide removes/installs the assembly and does not repair its internals. Record initial clutch lever free play 7-12 mm and control condition before removing any cable end.
verification: Engine identity, fault and lift/support plan recorded.

steps.title: Record the original cable positions
steps.instruction: Record the pull and return cable positions at the grip against the page 4-38 diagram. Record existing grip free play, which must be 3–6 mm before this service. Preserve the outer cable routing and adjustment so neither cable is swapped on refit.
verification: Pull/return identities, routing and initial free play recorded.

steps.title: Drain the engine oil before lifting
steps.instruction: For a normally running engine, follow the oil-change warm-up then stop the engine; do not run a faulted engine solely to warm oil. Stand the bike upright, place drain containers and remove the filler cap and both oil drain bolts. Drain tank and crankcase. Leave the oil filter unchanged unless separately serviced. Install new drain-bolt gaskets: tank bolt 10 N·m, crankcase bolt 20 N·m. Mark the engine empty of oil.
verification: Oil drained; two new gaskets; tank 10/crankcase 20 N·m; engine marked empty.

steps.title: Prepare the bike
steps.instruction: Stop the engine, let it cool and support the bike. Clean the intake and fuel work area. Keep dirt out of open joints and fuel work away from ignition sources.
verification: Cold engine; stable bike; clean work area; parts/tools ready.

steps.title: Open the sub-seat
steps.instruction: Release its quick fastener and lift the sub-seat first; it is tethered to the main seat. Open the fuel cap and transfer the tank fuel with a fuel-safe pump into a suitable container, then secure the cap.
verification: Sub-seat tether not strained; fuel contained.

steps.title: Remove access panels
steps.instruction: Remove the main-seat bolts and slide the seat rearward. Remove left/right side covers, keeping bolts and collars labeled. Slide the right cover projection out of its single locating slot as illustrated; do not pull the tab apart.
verification: Seat and two side covers removed; hardware locations retained.

steps.title: Isolate the battery
steps.instruction: With the engine stopped, disconnect the negative battery lead first, then the positive lead. Insulate the loose terminals. Retain the battery and relay in place unless separate frame work requires removal; no starter action is allowed during the work.
verification: Negative then positive disconnected and insulated.

steps.title: Expose the tank
steps.instruction: Release the air-filter-case cover ribs by pressing the duct sides inward and lifting the rear; slide the cover rearward to release the front projection. Leave the filter installed. Remove the left/right shroud bolts and shrouds, retaining their collars.
verification: Air-filter-case cover and shrouds removed; filter undisturbed.

steps.title: Disconnect the tank
steps.instruction: Unplug the fuel-pump connector. Put cloths below and around the fuel-hose joint for residual pressure. Remove the connector holder, slide the cover back, press its two release buttons and separate the joint by hand. Fit the supplied joint covers to both openings immediately.
verification: Pump disconnected; both fuel openings capped; no forced hose tools.

steps.title: Lift the tank clear
steps.instruction: Remove the tank mounting fasteners, retaining the collars/dampers in their original locations, and lift the tank away. Support it so its weight does not rest on the fuel-pump mounting surface. Leave the pump installed in the tank.
verification: Tank supported; mounts accounted for; pump untouched.

steps.title: Release the intact case
steps.instruction: Disconnect the intake-air-temperature-sensor coupler by its connector latch. Loosen the air-filter-case joint clamp screw and remove the three case mounting bolts, retaining their collars, washers and dampers at the original locations. Keep the filter, temperature sensor and case assembly bracket attached to the case. Identify and release the cylinder-head breather connection to the air-filter case if it prevents free removal; retain its spring clamp and protect the opening.
verification: Sensor coupler disconnected; three mounting sets retained; case internals attached.

steps.title: Lift off and protect the intake
steps.instruction: Lift the case clear of its seated intake connection without loading the remaining throttle body. Protect the exposed throttle-body inlet from dirt. Keep the case clean and inspect the joint and mounting supports for visible damage. Do not push the throttle valve, loosen sensor screws or move the cables.
verification: Intact case removed; clean inlet protected; throttle and sensors undisturbed.

steps.title: Open the cable housing
steps.instruction: Pull back the rubber cover. Remove the housing screws and separate the throttle cable housing without pulling on the cables.
verification: Housing open; rubber cover and screws retained.

steps.title: Release the two grip-end cables
steps.instruction: Disengage the pull and return cable ends from their original seats in the throttle tube as shown. Support the cables without kinking them and withdraw the complete grip/tube assembly from the bar. Do not peel the bonded rubber grip off its tube or disturb the cable ends at the throttle body.
verification: Both identified ends released; intact grip/tube retained.

steps.title: Check the released parts
steps.instruction: Inspect the tube sliding surface and cable-end seats for damage and check that the cables move without binding. Keep dirt out of the open housing. A damaged or frayed cable needs a separate full cable-renewal operation before this access job can return to service.
verification: Retained parts accepted; no damaged cable or binding.

steps.title: Remove the complete silencer
steps.instruction: Support the silencer. Loosen its joint clamp, remove its two mounting bolts and lift the complete silencer off its joint. Keep the silencer body, end cap and packing assembled.
verification: Complete silencer supported and removed; internals untouched.

steps.title: Remove the intermediate pipe
steps.instruction: Loosen the pipe-2 joint clamp and remove the exhaust-pipe bracket bolt while supporting the pipe. Move pipe 2 through the clearance path shown in PDF207 and remove it without forcing nearby components.
verification: Pipe 2 removed; mounting hardware retained.

steps.title: Remove the header and old seals
steps.instruction: Remove the header nuts and header pipe. Leave the header protector attached. Remove the old exhaust-port gasket at the cylinder head and the two pipe-joint gaskets; inspect joint faces and supports for damage before refitting.
verification: Header removed; all three separated joint seals identified; protector untouched.

steps.title: Set up for a cold drain
steps.instruction: Stand the cooled bike upright on a level surface. Place the collection container beneath the engine and position it close to the drain outlet, because flow can shoot sideways when the radiator cap is released.
verification: Bike stable; engine and coolant cold; collection ready.

steps.title: Open the drain and radiator cap
steps.instruction: Remove the coolant drain bolt and its copper washer. Place a thick cloth over the radiator cap and turn it slowly counterclockwise toward its detent to release residual pressure. Once hissing stops, press down and turn farther to remove the cap. Let the coolant drain into the container. Thoroughly flush the cooling system with clean tap water as Yamaha directs, then drain the flush water completely before fitting the new drain washer. Account for residual water when establishing the final coolant mixture.
verification: Drain complete; old washer removed; cap opened only when cold.

steps.title: Install a new drain washer
steps.instruction: Install a new copper washer and the coolant drain bolt. Tighten the bolt to 10 N·m.
verification: New washer installed; drain bolt 10 N·m.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Identify radiator hoses 1,3 and 4 from the source drawing. Mark each hose and clamp position, loosen its engine-side clamp and release the hoses from the engine. Keep radiators mounted and protect the open hose/engine ports from dirt. Do not remove coolant pipe joints or the temperature sensor itself.
verification: Hoses 1/3/4 labeled and clear; pipe joints/sensor remain sealed.

steps.title: Lift the intact throttle body from the engine joint
steps.instruction: Clean the lower intake joint, loosen its clamp and lift the intact throttle body clear. The grip-end cables were detached earlier; support the body and both identified cables separately outside the engine lifting path without tension. Keep body-end cable seats, sensors, adjustment screws and pulley intact; protect the engine intake and housing against dirt. The injector and sensor leads may remain connected while this group is supported next to the frame with slack; they must not carry its weight. Do not try to move it beyond their free reach.
verification: Throttle body supported clear; cables/sensors undisturbed; intake protected.

steps.title: Disconnect the left engine harness interfaces
steps.instruction: Release only the retaining clips/ties needed to free engine leads. Disconnect the stator, crankshaft-position and gear-position connectors; keep the gear-position switch bolted to the engine so its seal is not disturbed. Match connector identity to the diagrams, including the white 3-pin gear-position and gray 2-pin stator connectors. Label and protect both halves.
verification: Stator/crank-position/gear-position leads released; sensor seals untouched.

steps.title: Disconnect starter, ground and plug interfaces
steps.instruction: Disconnect the coolant-temperature connector, pull the spark-plug cap clear without removing the plug, and remove the engine-ground terminal bolt. At the starter lead, hold the motor-side terminal nut with a spanner while undoing the lead nut. Release the lead clamps and support the harness away from the lift path.
verification: Ground/starter/temperature/plug disconnected; starter terminal not twisted.

steps.title: Remove chain, sprocket and shift pedal
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel still secured, chain intact and rear brake still fully mounted, select neutral. Remove the cover and flatten the old lock-washer tabs. Have a helper hold the rear brake firmly while using a correctly fitting socket and manual breaker bar to loosen the sprocket nut, following the attributed Nick Dole technique. Do not use impact, heat or jam the chain against the case. Once loose, release the stock chain joint and remove the chain, retaining its matched link/plate and preparing a new clip. Remove the nut, old lock washer and sprocket. Mark and remove the shift pedal, preserving punch-mark alignment.
verification: Chain and sprocket clear; old lock washer/clip retired; shift position recorded.

steps.title: Disconnect and record the cable clutch
steps.instruction: Record clutch lever free play and the cable-end/adjuster positions. Release cable tension with the handlebar adjuster as necessary. Disconnect the engine-end cable nipple from the push lever and release the cable outer from its bracket as shown in the inset; keep the push lever, shaft and clutch cover installed. Retain the cable with its handlebar lever and support it clear of the engine lifting path. This bike has a cable clutch.
verification: Engine-end nipple and outer detached and identified; push lever and clutch internals remain installed; cable supported.

steps.title: Clear pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard, brake-pedal pivot bolt and return spring. Support the pedal with its master-cylinder linkage attached. Label and release the cylinder-head breather hose from the engine and its routing holders. Keep brake hydraulics closed.
verification: Guard/pedal/spring retained; breather clear; brake system closed.

steps.title: Support engine and swingarm before undoing mounts
steps.instruction: Support the engine independently. Support the swingarm and prepare a same-diameter temporary support shaft from its other side if needed when the pivot is withdrawn. Confirm every electrical connector, hose, intake assembly and cable is clear before loosening the engine mounts.
verification: Independent supports ready; all engine interfaces clear.

steps.title: Release the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Remove the left/right upper brackets and two lower brackets with their identified hardware, keeping bolt positions separate. Withdraw the pivot while maintaining swingarm support. Keep the engine fully supported as the last mounting fasteners come out; never let it hang from a remaining hose or lead.
verification: Mount hardware mapped; pivot removed with swingarm supported.

steps.title: Lift the engine out to the right
steps.instruction: Lift the engine and move its lower part toward the right side of the chassis as shown in the OEM drawing, then transfer it to the prepared support. Stop if any interface catches. Keep the inlet, exhaust and fluid ports protected from contamination.
verification: Assembly removed to right; no trapped interface; engine stable.

steps.title: Confirm the engine is ready for bench work
steps.instruction: Confirm exact standard US 2025 YZ450F stock engine, cold at room temperature, drained and securely supported after the preceding engine-removal steps. Intake, exhaust, coolant and electrical interfaces must be clear. Keep the lower engine assembled until the head, cylinder and piston have been removed in the following steps. The lower-engine sequence then opens and closes the supported stock systems before top-end assembly resumes. Plan the head repair and later installation/commissioning before opening the engine.
verification: Engine identity, condition and access handoff recorded.
steps.composition_adaptation: Explicit combined lower/top-end component state and exact OEM break-in groups; source mechanics retained.

steps.title: Expose the valve train
steps.instruction: Clean around the plug before removing it. Disconnect the head breather and remove plug, head-cover bolts, cover, top chain guide and old cover/plug-hole gaskets. Keep the breather plate and its mounts intact. Protect the open engine from dirt.
verification: Cover hardware and top guide retained; sealing surfaces protected.

steps.title: Open the timing inspection ports
steps.instruction: Remove the timing-mark and crankshaft-end access screws and their O-rings. Keep their identities separate.
verification: Both ports open; screws identified.

steps.title: Set the cold measurement position
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise by hand. Align the rotor TDC mark with the cover mark and verify both cam-sprocket marks align with the cam-cap surface edges in the diagram. Do not force resistance or rely on the rotor mark alone.
verification: Rotor and both cam marks recorded.

steps.title: Measure the four valve clearances
steps.instruction: Use a feeler gauge at each illustrated cam/lifter gap with the engine cold at room temperature and piston at the confirmed TDC position. Record intake left/right and exhaust left/right. Intake is 0.10–0.17 mm; exhaust 0.15–0.22 mm. These readings establish the pre-repair condition, not final acceptance.
verification: All four cold readings and positions saved.

steps.title: Remove the chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Remove the tensioner cap bolt, tensioner mounting bolts, tensioner and gaskets. Retain the chain position; keep the crank at the established position.
verification: Tensioner removed and sealing pieces identified.

steps.title: Lift out the cams
steps.instruction: Loosen cap bolts evenly in a crisscross pattern from outside inward, then remove caps and cams. Label intake/exhaust, caps, dowels and hardware. Wire the chain securely so it cannot fall into the crankcase. Do not turn the crank with the cams being removed.
verification: Cams/caps kept in matched positions; chain supported.

steps.title: Inspect the tensioner
steps.instruction: Reject cracks or damage. With light finger pressure on the rod, use a thin screwdriver to wind it fully clockwise. Release the screwdriver while maintaining light pressure: the rod must extend smoothly. Replace the complete tensioner if it fails.
verification: Condition and smooth-extension result recorded.

steps.title: Release and lift the head
steps.instruction: Use the removal diagram on this page, which is different from the tightening numbering. Loosen each bolt half a turn per pass in illustrated order 1–6 until all are loose, then remove them. The two small bolts are M6×45 mm and four main bolts M10×129 mm. Lift the head, retain dowels and intake-side chain guide, and remove the head gasket while keeping the chain supported. Leave head studs and oil-passage plugs installed.
verification: Head removed; removal order followed and chain retained.

steps.title: Inspect the head and intake chain guide
steps.instruction: Remove carbon with a rounded scraper, avoiding plug threads and sealing faces; remove deposits/rust from coolant passages. Inspect head damage/scratches and guide wear/damage; replace a damaged guide. Measure head warpage with straightedge and feeler gauge across the illustrated directions: limit 0.05 mm. This route retains a sound original head and excludes resurfacing or replacement of a damaged head.
verification: Warpage readings, head condition and chain-guide disposition saved.

steps.title: Lift off the cylinder
steps.instruction: Remove the cylinder bolt, lift the cylinder while retaining chain/guide through its cavity, and collect the base gasket and two dowels. Support the exposed piston and cover the crankcase opening.
verification: Cylinder removed and crankcase opening protected.

steps.title: Remove piston and rings
steps.instruction: Cover the case opening before removing pin clips. Deburr the clip groove and pin bore area if needed; never hammer the pin. If it remains tight use the specified piston-pin puller. Remove pin and piston. Spread each ring only enough by hand to lift its opposite side over the crown, keeping top, second and oil rings identified.
verification: Piston/rings identified; no clip or debris lost.

steps.title: Confirm the lower-engine bench handoff
steps.instruction: Confirm the exact stock US 2025 YZ450F engine is cold, fully drained, removed and securely supported. Head, cylinder, piston and cams are already removed and separately indexed; the timing chain is retained. External clutch cable, coolant, exhaust and electrical connections are disconnected. This operation services crankcases, complete crankshaft assembly, gearbox and their required drives. It retains intact water-pump, pressure-relief and starter-motor internals. Resolve faults in those excluded systems before proceeding. Account for and remove the protective cloth placed below the piston before opening the cases. Restore clean opening protection as needed between operations; account for every cloth before closure.
verification: Identity, drained condition, removed top end and excluded-system condition recorded.

steps.title: Remove the generator cover
steps.instruction: Record left-cover bolts and lead-holder positions. Remove the eight cover bolts, lift the cover with its stator and position sensor still installed, and retain two dowels. Remove the old gasket. Protect the lead and keep the cover supported without loading its wiring; do not disturb the stator, sensor or sealed grommet.
verification: Cover assembly and hardware indexed; stator mounts remain intact.

steps.title: Remove the rotor
steps.instruction: Hold the illustrated rotor flats while loosening the rotor nut. Remove nut and washer. Use rotor puller 90890-04151 / YM-04151 to release the rotor; retain the Woodruff key. Do not pry against the stator or sealing surface.
verification: Rotor, key and washer retained without taper damage.

steps.title: Remove the clutch spring and plate pack
steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover and old gasket. Loosen the six pressure-plate bolts evenly, then remove pressure plate 1, clutch spring, spring retainer and pressure plate 2. Remove pushrod 1 with its bearing/circlip and the ball. Index the two thin end steels, seven thicker steels, eight friction plates and six collars by type and position.
verification: Plate/spring stack and release parts indexed.

steps.title: Remove the clutch boss and primary driven gear
steps.instruction: Straighten the clutch-boss nut stake. Hold the boss with holder sleeve 90890-04199 / YM-91042 and remove the nut. Remove spacer, washer, sleeve, six absorbers, boss, washer, primary driven gear, collar, idle gear and its washer in the illustrated order. The removed staked nut will not be reused.
verification: All spacers, washers and absorbers retained in order.

steps.title: Remove the right cover and filter
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover, element and O-ring, and remove the filler cap and O-ring. Remove the ten right-cover bolts, cover, two dowels and gasket. Keep the complete water pump and the right-cover check-ball seat intact. Replace the removed filter, O-rings and cover gasket during closure.
verification: Right cover removed; retained water pump/check-ball assemblies protected.

steps.title: Clear the clutch release from the case
steps.instruction: Remove the push-lever shaft, two release mounting bolts and complete release assembly, then withdraw pushrod 2. Keep the shaft bearings and seals intact for inspection; retain the pushrod washer and discard the removed O-ring. Do not confuse the cable-operated release with a hydraulic release.
verification: Release and pushrod removed; seal and bearing condition accessible.

steps.title: Remove the external shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Remove shift shaft, collar, return spring and roller, then guide/lever and their two pawls, pins and springs. Remove stopper and spring. Turn the segment counterclockwise until it stops before loosening its bolt; do not use an impact wrench. Remove the segment and protect its locating features.
verification: Small shift parts and segment indexed.

steps.title: Remove the primary and balancer drives
steps.instruction: Flatten the balancer lock-washer tab. Place an aluminum plate between the illustrated drive/driven teeth to hold them while loosening the primary and balancer nuts. Remove primary nut/washer/gear/collar, starter reduction gear, circlip, starter clutch and balancer drive gear; remove balancer nut, old lock washer, driven gear and oil-pump drive gear. Preserve their order and the timing marks. Remove the damper holder, damper and washer for unrestricted case/bearing work.
verification: Gear stacks and damper indexed; holding plate removed.

steps.title: Remove and strip the oil pump
steps.instruction: Remove the oil-pump assembly. Index outer/inner rotor 1, its dowel and washer/circlip, then remove the pump cover, outer/inner rotor 2, dowel and shaft. Leave the pressure-relief ball, spring and pressed seat installed. Keep both rotor sets and dowels distinct.
verification: Pump parts indexed; pressure-relief internals remain assembled.

steps.title: Remove the lower timing-chain parts
steps.instruction: Remove exhaust-side chain guide, guide stopper plate and timing chain. Retain the guide pivot hardware in order. The top-end parts must already be off; do not pull a trapped chain through assembled cams. Inspect chain stiffness and guide wear/damage now. A stiff chain requires camshaft sprockets, chain and crankshaft sprocket renewed as a set; the crank sprocket is supplied with the complete crankshaft. Record this before selecting the crank assembly, and arrange matching cam/sprocket renewal for later top-end closure. Replace a failed guide.
verification: Chain/guide condition and matched-set replacement decision recorded before crank selection.

steps.title: Separate the crankcases
steps.instruction: Identify the nine case bolts by length and location in the diagram. Loosen each one a quarter turn per pass until all are loose, then remove them. Place the left case downward. Use the designated splitting slit and light soft-hammer taps on reinforced bosses to release the joint; do not pry at mating faces or force separation. Lift the right half horizontally, leaving crank and transmission in the left half. Remove dowels and O-ring.
verification: Cases separated without forced mating-face damage.

steps.title: Remove the transmission
steps.instruction: Remove long/short guide bars with all four springs, shift drum and the three forks, keeping their direction and position recorded. Lift main and drive shafts together; if needed lightly tap the drive shaft with a soft hammer. Keep the drive collar in the case until the assembly is clear, then retain it separately.
verification: Both shafts, forks, bars, springs and drum indexed.

steps.title: Remove the balancer and crank assembly
steps.instruction: Turn the balancer flat toward the crank and withdraw it. Use crankcase separating tool 90890-04152 / YU-A9642 as illustrated to remove the complete crankshaft assembly. Do not hammer the crank ends or separate the pressed crank assembly.
verification: Complete crankshaft and balancer removed.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the cases and oil routes
steps.instruction: Remove oil strainer, its two bolts, old O-ring and the illustrated small gasket. Remove the two oil nozzles, preserving their identities. Clean gasket residue and cases with mild solvent; inspect for cracks and damage. Clear all cleaning solvent and debris and dry the cases before assembly. Clean oil passages with compressed air while controlling debris; never spin bearings with compressed air. Damaged cases require a correctly matched replacement case set and inspection of all fits, outside this retained-case route.
verification: Clean passages, strainer/nozzles and sound retained cases accepted.

steps.title: Inspect and renew case bearings as needed
steps.instruction: Check each case bearing for roughness, wear or damage. For a failed bearing remove its illustrated retainer and drive it out by the inner race; discard it. Install the exact replacement parallel by pressing only the outer race, oiling the bearing and keeping its marked/size face outward. Follow the individual left/right diagrams: each illustrated bearing seating depth is 0 mm at its own shown datum. Refit crank-bearing retaining screws at 30 N·m with LOCTITE; other illustrated retaining plates at 12 N·m with LOCTITE. Do not invent a preload or drive against balls/rollers.
verification: Bearing decisions, individual seating depths and retainer torques recorded.

steps.title: Renew the drive-shaft case seal
steps.instruction: Fit the correct new drive-shaft oil seal with lithium-soap-based grease on its lips and the main lip facing the oil chamber. Seat to 0–0.5 mm at the illustrated case datum. Protect the seal lip when its collar is later inserted.
verification: Drive-shaft seal depth measured and recorded.

steps.title: Inspect the crankshaft and balancer
steps.instruction: Support and slowly rotate the crank as illustrated while measuring runout with a dial gauge: maximum 0.030 mm. Measure assembly width: 61.93–62.00 mm. Inspect the crank sprocket for wear/damage and clear oil passages with compressed air. Failed runout, width or sprocket condition requires replacement of the complete crank assembly. Inspect the balancer for damage. This route does not press apart the connecting-rod assembly or specify a rod-rebuild process.
verification: Runout, width and complete-assembly disposition recorded.

steps.title: Inspect shafts, gears and shifting parts
steps.instruction: Measure both shaft runouts on centers with a dial gauge: maximum 0.08 mm each. Reject pitted, blue, worn gears or chipped/rounded dogs; replace the affected gears. Inspect forks at followers and pawls and check bars on a flat surface; never straighten a bent bar. Rough fork/bar movement requires replacement of the fork and bar together. Replace a worn/damaged drum assembly. Record every retained and replaced part.
verification: Shaft runouts and all gear/fork/bar/drum decisions recorded.

steps.title: Rebuild the shaft stacks
steps.instruction: Use the exact exploded stack and sectional diagrams for every gear, collar, washer and circlip. Main-shaft gear counts are 22/20/21/16 teeth in the illustrated stack; drive-shaft stack uses 26/21/27/25/28 teeth. Apply molybdenum disulfide oil to idler-gear/collar inner and end faces and sliding-gear inner faces, and engine oil where separately illustrated. Use new circlips with the sharp edge away from the adjacent washer/gear and their ends evenly on spline crests; do not overexpand them. Fit the new illustrated drive-shaft O-ring with lithium-soap-based grease. Each gear must move smoothly before installation.
verification: Exact gear/washer/collar orientations and circlip seating accepted.

steps.title: Install the crank and balancer
steps.instruction: Grease seal lips with lithium-soap-based grease and apply molybdenum disulfide grease to both the crankshaft and balancer-shaft locations indicated by the arrows in the diagram. Use crank installer pot 90890-01274 / YU-90058, bolt 90890-01275 / YU-90060, M12 adapter 90890-01278 / YU-90063 and spacer 90890-04081 / YM-91044. Hold the rod at TDC and draw the crank into its bearing until fully seated, using the tool rather than hammering. Fit the balancer with its flat toward the crank.
verification: Crank fully seated and balancer installed without impact.

steps.title: Install the transmission and forks
steps.instruction: Grease the drive-collar seal lip and install its collar without folding the lip. Oil case bearings and install main and drive shafts together into the left case. Install fork 1 marked L onto the fifth wheel gear, fork 3 marked R onto the fourth wheel, and fork 2 marked C onto the third pinion. Oil fork grooves and drum groove/bearing; install the drum in the illustrated orientation.
verification: Correct fork markings, gear engagement and drum position confirmed.

steps.title: Fit guide bars and test shifting
steps.instruction: Lightly screw the four springs into the ends of their correct long/short guide bars, oil the bars and install them as illustrated. Operate the drum and rotate the shafts to verify all forks, gears and shifting move smoothly. Do not close the case over binding or incomplete engagement.
verification: Shift/rotation check passed across all selected positions.

steps.title: Restore the oil nozzles and strainer
steps.instruction: Install the right-case oil nozzle with its bolt at 10 N·m and LOCTITE. Install the separate left-case threaded oil nozzle at 0.5 N·m. Fit the clean accepted strainer, new illustrated small gasket and new strainer O-ring with lithium-soap-based grease; tighten the two strainer bolts to 10 N·m with LOCTITE.
verification: Nozzles and strainer restored with correct separate preparations.

steps.title: Seal and join the cases
steps.instruction: Account for all tools, cloths and loose parts. Fit dowels and new illustrated O-ring. Apply ThreeBond 1215 to the mating surface path shown in the diagram, keeping passages clear. Hold the rod at TDC, lower the right case onto the left and seat it with light soft-hammer taps only. Match the nine bolts to the 45/60/75 mm length map. Tighten crisscross to 12 N·m in two stages, quarter-turn increments. Confirm crank and transmission still move freely after tightening.
verification: Case bolt map/torque and post-closure free movement recorded.

steps.title: Restore the timing chain and guide
steps.instruction: Confirm the chain/guide decisions recorded before case splitting were implemented. If stiffness required a matched set, the installed crankshaft must already have the new sprocket and matching cam/sprocket parts must be reserved for top-end closure. Never pair a fresh chain with failed retained sprockets. Install the accepted chain, guide and stopper plate in their illustrated positions. Tighten the guide pivot bolt to 12 N·m and stopper plate bolt to 10 N·m with LOCTITE. Retain the chain securely for the separate top-end installation.
verification: Chain/guide decisions and matched-sprocket requirement recorded; guide secured and chain retained.

steps.title: Inspect the oil-pump parts
steps.instruction: Inspect both rotor sets, shaft, cover and housing for cracks, damage or wear. Replace the complete pump if damaged or if it fails smooth movement after correct reassembly. Keep the retained pressure-relief seat/ball/spring undisturbed; a suspected relief fault requires its separate repair before engine use.
verification: Pump condition and retained relief-system decision recorded.

steps.title: Assemble and install the pump
steps.instruction: Oil shaft, rotor set 2 and its dowel; engage the dowel with the inner-rotor slit and fit the cover at 6 N·m with LOCTITE. Fit washer, dowel and oiled rotor set 1 with a new circlip, ensuring the pin engages its groove. Install the assembly at 5 N·m with LOCTITE. Verify smooth rotation after each fastening stage; failed movement must be corrected before proceeding.
verification: Rotor/dowel engagement, 6/5 N·m and smooth rotation recorded.

steps.title: Inspect the drive gears and starter clutch
steps.instruction: Inspect both primary drive and driven gears: damage or wear of either gear, abnormal primary-gear noise or excessive free play requires replacement of primary drive and driven gears together. Inspect balancer gears separately and replace failed balancer parts. Inspect the starter clutch for burrs, chipped teeth, roughness or wear and replace the complete failed assembly. Fit it with the balancer drive and reduction gear for a functional check: turning the balancer drive counterclockwise must freewheel; clockwise must engage.
verification: Gear dispositions and directional starter-clutch check recorded.

steps.title: Restore the timed balancer drive
steps.instruction: Install oil-pump drive gear and balancer driven gear with their lower splines aligned to the shaft. Install balancer drive gear with its lower spline aligned to the crank and align the punched drive/driven timing marks exactly. Fit a new lock washer and tighten the balancer nut to 50 N·m using the aluminum holding plate as illustrated. Bend the locking tab after tightening.
verification: Balancer timing marks and 50 N·m locking recorded.

steps.title: Restore starter clutch and primary drive
steps.instruction: Oil the starter clutch and fit its manufacturer mark outward, then a new circlip, starter reduction gear with oil on its inner/contact faces, collar, primary gear and washer. Apply molybdenum disulfide grease to the washer contact and primary-nut threads/contact surface. With the aluminum plate in the illustrated holding position, tighten the primary nut to 130 N·m. Remove the holding plate. Restore damper, washer and holder with two bolts at 12 N·m and LOCTITE.
verification: 130 N·m preparation/torque and damper closure recorded.

steps.title: Inspect the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Reject bent/worn shaft, damaged spring, guide, lever, pawls, pins or springs. Inspect stopper and its spring and replace failed parts. Ensure replacement parts match the original stock configuration.
verification: Shift-mechanism parts accepted.

steps.title: Restore segment and pawls
steps.instruction: Install stopper, collar and spring with the stopper bolt at 10 N·m and LOCTITE. Align the segment projections with the drum slits while pressing the stopper down; tighten the segment bolt to 30 N·m with LOCTITE as marked in the exploded diagram. Oil the two pawl springs, pins and pawls; install lever and guide together, then guide bolts at 10 N·m with LOCTITE.
verification: Segment location, pawls and separate fasteners confirmed.

steps.title: Restore the shift shaft and seal
steps.instruction: Fit the correct new shift-shaft seal with lithium-soap-based grease on its lips, seating depth 0–1 mm at the illustrated datum. Oil the shaft, then fit dowel/roller, return spring and collar in the diagram positions. Confirm return action and shifting while rotating the transmission by hand.
verification: Seal depth and shift-return function recorded.

steps.title: Inspect the clutch release and pushrods
steps.instruction: Inspect push-lever shaft, pushrods 1 and 2, bearing and ball for wear, cracks or damage. Check pushrod 2 bending: maximum 0.10 mm. This route retains sound release bearings and seals; failed internal bearings/seals require the separate renewal operation before continuing. Replace damaged pushrods/ball or complete matching release parts as applicable.
verification: Pushrod bending and release condition accepted.

steps.title: Refit the cable clutch release
steps.instruction: Oil the retained shaft bearings and apply lithium-soap-based grease to seal lips. Fit pushrod 2 with its washer and a new O-ring lubricated with lithium-soap-based grease. Restore the complete release with bolts at 10 N·m and LOCTITE, then install the push-lever shaft. Keep the cable disconnected until engine refitting.
verification: Release and pushrod installed; cable remains for frame closure.

steps.title: Refit the right cover
steps.instruction: Inspect the retained right-cover seal/check-ball seat and water-pump assembly for damage before closure; this route does not disturb their internals. Fit two dowels and a new right-cover gasket, align the retained components and install the ten bolts in their original length positions. Tighten in stages crisscross to 10 N·m.
verification: Right cover seated with new gasket and intact retained assemblies.

steps.title: Install a new filter
steps.instruction: Install the correct new filter element in the illustrated orientation and a new filter-cover O-ring lubricated with lithium-soap-based grease. Refit the filter cover and tighten both bolts to 10 N·m. Fit the filler cap with a new O-ring lubricated with lithium-soap-based grease to protect the engine; fluid filling belongs to the later engine-refit operation. Record that this engine was disassembled and the filter renewed.
verification: New filter and O-ring installed; cover 10 N·m and disassembly condition recorded.

steps.title: Inspect clutch friction and release parts
steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four places: standard 2.12–2.28 mm, limit 2.02 mm; replace the friction set if failed. Check every steel plate on a flat surface with a feeler gauge: warpage maximum 0.10 mm; replace the steel set if failed. Measure clutch spring free height: standard 5.80 mm, minimum 5.51 mm. Replace damaged retainer/pressure plates; replace the collar set if worn/pitted. Inspect boss/driven dogs, sleeves and absorbers and replace damaged parts rather than inventing a material-removal allowance.
verification: Friction/steel/spring measurements and replacement decisions recorded.

steps.title: Restore the clutch base stack
steps.instruction: Fit washer, idle gear, collar, primary driven gear, washer, boss, six absorbers, sleeve, washer and spacer in the exact diagram order. Oil the mainshaft, specified washer faces, collar inner face, driven-gear inner/contact surfaces, absorber surfaces, sleeve inner/contact face and spacer faces. Do not trap the washer on the spacer step.
verification: All washers, spacers and absorbers correctly located.

steps.title: Secure the clutch boss
steps.instruction: Apply LOCTITE to the correct new boss nut and tighten to 105 N·m using holder sleeve 90890-04199 / YM-91042. Check that the washer rotates freely, then stake the nut into the mainshaft cutouts. The neighboring oiled spacer/washer stack does not change the nut locking-agent instruction.
verification: 105 N·m, free washer and stake recorded.

steps.title: Build the plate pack
steps.instruction: Oil six collars, all friction plates and steel plates. Follow the exact pack diagram: the two 1.0 mm steels are the two extreme end plates, the seven 1.4 mm steels alternate internally with eight frictions. The four blue-marked friction plates form two at each end of the friction sequence; the four unmarked frictions occupy its center. Preserve the illustrated pawl/paint orientation and do not interchange the thin end steels with internal steels.
verification: Exact end plates and painted/unpainted friction sequence confirmed.

steps.title: Install the release ball and clutch spring
steps.instruction: Oil the bearing and fit a new circlip on pushrod 1; oil the ball and rod and install them. Fit pressure plate 2, spring retainer, clutch spring in the engine-side orientation shown, then pressure plate 1. Oil the six bolt threads/contact surfaces and the illustrated pressure-plate contact. Tighten every bolt crisscross to 4 N·m first, then every bolt crisscross to 10 N·m.
verification: Spring orientation and 4 then 10 N·m stages recorded.

steps.title: Close the clutch
steps.instruction: Install a new clutch-cover gasket and restore the two long/four short bolts according to the diagram. Tighten in stages crisscross to 10 N·m. Keep external cable adjustment for the engine-refit operation.
verification: Clutch cover sealed and fastened.

steps.title: Inspect and install the rotor
steps.instruction: Inspect rotor inner surface and stator outer surface for damage; damage requires crank runout/bearing assessment before reuse. Replace a damaged key. Clean both crank and rotor tapers. Fit the Woodruff key with its flat parallel to the crank centerline, align the rotor keyway and seat the rotor. Fit washer and nut and hold the illustrated flats to tighten the nut to 65 N·m.
verification: Tapers, key alignment and 65 N·m recorded.

steps.title: Close the generator
steps.instruction: Confirm stator/sensor mounts and lead grommet remained intact. Fit two dowels and a new gasket, then cover and lead holder in recorded positions. Tighten eight bolts in stages crisscross to 10 N·m. Fit the oil-tank drain with a new gasket at 10 N·m and crankcase drain with a new gasket at 20 N·m if they were left out after draining.
verification: Generator cover and both drained-oil closures secured.

steps.title: Record the lower-engine handoff
steps.instruction: Record installed crank/gear/bearing/clutch/pump parts, all measurements, gear and balancer timing, torque preparations, seal depths, free movement and new filter. Keep the timing chain supported and cylinder opening clean. This engine remains without its top end and oil fill: complete the exact 2025 top-end assembly, engine refit, oil/coolant restoration and commissioning before any start. Disassembled oil quantity is 1.20 L, subject to the later verified level/flow checks; do not start a dry bench engine.
verification: Lower bench work accepted; top-end/refit/commissioning still outstanding.

steps.title: Measure the cylinder
steps.instruction: Inspect cylinder and piston walls for vertical scratches. Measure side-to-side and front-to-back at the three illustrated heights, recording D1–D6; C is their maximum. Standard bore 97.000–97.010 mm, wear limit 97.060 mm. Scratched walls require cylinder replacement and piston/rings as a set. This route supports exact stock replacement, not rebore or replating.
verification: Six bore readings and wall condition recorded.

steps.title: Measure piston diameter and actual clearance
steps.instruction: Measure piston diameter on the illustrated axis 9.0 mm above the skirt bottom: standard 96.955–96.970 mm. Calculate actual C minus piston diameter. The manual separately specifies 0.010–0.045 mm clearance and 0.15 mm limit. Preserve both stated ranges: individually acceptable diameters do not automatically establish an acceptable pair. Resolve a failing actual fit with the prescribed cylinder/piston/ring set replacement and remeasurement.
verification: Piston diameter, datum, actual subtraction and fit disposition saved.

steps.title: Measure ring side clearances
steps.instruction: Clean carbon from grooves and rings before measuring. Top standard side clearance is 0.015–0.065 mm, limit 0.120 mm; second standard is 0.020–0.060 mm, limit 0.100 mm. An out-of-specification result requires piston and rings as a set.
verification: Top and second side-clearance readings and parts decisions saved.

steps.title: Measure ring end gaps
steps.instruction: Square each ring near the cylinder bottom using the piston crown as illustrated. Record top and second end gaps: limits 0.55 mm and 0.85 mm respectively. Replace an out-of-specification ring. The oil expander gap is not measurable; if oil-rail gap is excessive replace the oil-ring set. No numerical oil-rail acceptance or ring filing amount is supplied here.
verification: Measured gaps and ring disposition saved; unresolved oil-rail condition not accepted by an invented limit.

steps.title: Inspect piston pin and bore
steps.instruction: A blue or grooved pin requires replacement and investigation of the lubrication system before this route can continue. Measure pin outside diameter (minimum 17.981 mm) and piston pin bore (maximum 18.045 mm). Replace pin or piston for the corresponding failed measurement. Also record the actual pin-to-bore clearance against the listed 0.004–0.024 mm range.
verification: Pin/bore measurements, actual clearance and surface condition saved.

steps.title: Accept the actual piston assembly
steps.instruction: Record the exact stock parts retained or renewed. All required cylinder, piston, ring and pin checks must pass on the final chosen parts before assembly. Do not treat wear limits as an invented new-part target or infer correct fit from catalog sizes. Lubrication faults, unidentified parts and unresolved measured fit stop this route.
verification: Final measured assembly and replacement decisions accepted.

steps.title: Identify each lifter and pad
steps.instruction: On the removed head, protect the chain opening with a cloth and use the valve lapper to lift each lifter and pad. Store and label all four pairs by original position. Keep the original cams and caps matched to this head.
verification: Four lifter/pad positions recorded.

steps.title: Check valve sealing before stripping
steps.instruction: Pour clean solvent into intake and exhaust ports as illustrated and check for leakage through each seat. The source identifies kerosene in its leakage check. Record leakage and inspect the associated face, seat and contact width; dispose of the solvent before further work.
verification: Four seat-sealing observations saved.

steps.title: Remove the valve assemblies
steps.instruction: Use the valve spring compressor and 22 mm attachment to compress each spring and remove its cotters. Release the compressor, then remove retainer, spring, valve, old stem seal and spring seat. Keep every part identified by valve position.
verification: All parts indexed and removed seals set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Inspect and measure valves and guides
steps.instruction: Measure each guide ID and stem OD and subtract to obtain actual clearance. Guide ID is 5.500–5.512 mm; minimum stem OD intake 5.445 mm/exhaust 5.435 mm. Clearance limits intake 0.080 mm/exhaust 0.100 mm. Inspect faces and stem ends; reject mushroomed ends. Measure stem runout on supports with a dial gauge: maximum 0.020 mm. Do not accept an undersize stem merely because clearance passes.
verification: Four ID/OD/clearance/runout results and condition decisions saved.

steps.title: Measure seat contact
steps.instruction: Remove carbon and inspect seats. Apply blue layout fluid to each valve face, press the valve through its guide against the seat, remove it and measure the contact band where blueing was displaced. Contact width limit is 1.5 mm for both intake and exhaust. Pitting/wear or failed original seat width requires head replacement under the inspection instructions and is outside this retained-head route.
verification: Four contact widths and seat condition saved.

steps.title: Inspect springs and lifters
steps.instruction: Measure spring free lengths: intake minimum 36.65 mm, exhaust minimum 37.34 mm. Replace failed springs with correct stock parts. Damaged or scratched lifters require lifters and cylinder head together; do not fit a fresh lifter into a failed head in this route.
verification: Spring measurements, lifter condition and decisions saved.

steps.title: Choose retained valves or guide renewal
steps.instruction: Continue into guide renewal only with a sound retained head, acceptable seats and lifters, appropriate replacement parts and arranged specialist seat refacing. A new running valve always requires a new guide; new valves used for lapping must be replaced by distinct new running valves. If all original valves/guides/seats passed and no lapping or machining is needed, choose the retained-valve branch instead.
verification: Repair path and component decisions recorded.

branches.label: Retain all four accepted original valves and guides
branches.condition: All original valve, guide, seat, sealing and lifter checks pass; no lapping or machining is required.

steps.title: Prepare the guide-renewal parts
steps.instruction: For every guide/valve position being renewed, identify the correct new guide, a new valve used only for lapping and a distinct new valve for running. Keep the running valves away from lapping compound. Preserve unaffected original parts only if their recorded checks passed. Arrange professional seat refacing; this guide does not specify cutter angles or a machining allowance.
verification: Renewal positions, separate lapping/running valves and refacing service recorded.

steps.title: Heat the head and remove the guides
steps.instruction: Heat the stripped head to 100 °C in an oven to preserve the guide fit. Support it securely and use the 5.5 mm guide remover in the illustrated direction to remove each selected guide. Handle the heated head with suitable protection.
verification: Head temperature and guides removed recorded.

steps.title: Install the new guides
steps.instruction: Use the illustrated guide installer and remover to drive each new guide to its measured installation height from the shown head datum. Intake height 13.5–13.9 mm; exhaust 12.2–12.6 mm. Keep intake/exhaust locations distinct.
verification: Each guide height measured and recorded.

steps.title: Ream and measure the new guides
steps.instruction: Use the specified 5.5 mm reamer after installation. Measure actual guide ID, new running-valve stem OD and clearance for every renewed position. Apply the same 5.500–5.512 mm ID, intake/exhaust minimum stem diameters 5.445/5.435 mm and clearance limits 0.080/0.100 mm. Confirm the running valves also pass the 0.020 mm runout check; remove all machining debris.
verification: New guide/running-valve measurements and cleanliness accepted.

steps.title: Have the seats refaced for the new guides
steps.instruction: Have a qualified cylinder-head specialist reface every seat associated with a renewed guide before lapping. Record the actual completed service and resulting seat condition. Cutter selection, angles and material removal are not prescribed here; do not mark an arranged appointment as completed work.
verification: Actual specialist refacing record and accepted seat condition attached.

steps.title: Lap with the sacrificial new valves
steps.instruction: Use only the new lapping valves assigned to the renewed positions. Apply coarse compound to the face and molybdenum disulfide oil to the stem; keep compound out of the stem-to-guide gap. Insert the valve and turn it with the lapper, using the illustrated tap-and-lap action until contact is evenly polished. Remove all compound from face and seat.
verification: Coarse lapping completed without contaminating guides.

steps.title: Finish lapping and recheck contact
steps.instruction: Repeat with fine compound and clean all compound away after every lapping stage. Apply blue layout fluid, press the valve into its seat, remove and measure the contact band again. Maximum contact width is 1.5 mm. If contact remains out of specification, return for refacing and repeat the lapping/measurement sequence before proceeding.
verification: Final renewed-seat widths and contact accepted.

steps.title: Separate lapping valves from running parts
steps.instruction: Remove all sacrificial lapping valves from the running-parts tray. Use the distinct new running valves for renewed positions; do not install a valve used for lapping into the running engine. Clean the head and confirm the final running-valve/guide measurements remain accepted.
verification: Running-valve identities and discarded lapping valves recorded.

steps.title: Install valves and new stem seals
steps.instruction: Clean stem ends; lubricate stems and all new stem seals with molybdenum disulfide oil. Fit each spring seat, new stem seal, accepted valve, spring and retainer. Original retained parts return to their original positions; renewed parts go to their recorded positions. Install springs with the larger pitch upward.
verification: Four valve assemblies seated with new seals and correct spring orientation.

steps.title: Secure the cotters
steps.instruction: Compress each spring with the specified tool and 22 mm attachment and install its cotters. Release the tool, then lightly tap each valve tip with a soft-face hammer to seat the cotters. Excessive impact can damage the valve.
verification: Cotters seated in all four assemblies.

steps.title: Confirm final valve sealing
steps.instruction: Repeat the illustrated clean-solvent port check on the assembled head, including the actual new running valves where fitted. A leaking seat cannot proceed to engine assembly; resolve the seat/valve condition and repeat acceptance. After acceptance, drain the test solvent and dry the ports before engine assembly.
verification: Four final running-valve sealing results accepted.

steps.title: Return the pads and lifters
steps.instruction: Apply engine oil to pads and lifters, return each to its identified location and verify every lifter rotates smoothly with a finger. Preserve the pad numbers and original positions for final clearance adjustment.
verification: Four pads/lifters installed in their identified positions.

steps.title: Measure cam lobes
steps.instruction: Inspect for blue discoloration, pitting and scratches. Measure each lobe height on the illustrated axis: intake minimum 38.030 mm and exhaust minimum 34.170 mm. A failed cam needs replacement; this route continues only with accepted exact stock cams and a serviceable matching head/caps.
verification: Lobe readings and cam surface decisions saved.

steps.title: Measure the cam journals in the head
steps.instruction: Place cams in the head, position Plastigauge on the illustrated journals, install dowels and matching caps, and tighten caps crisscross from inner to outer at 10 N·m. Do not turn the cams during measurement. Remove caps evenly and read the flattened strips. Required clearance is 0.028–0.062 mm. Clean off the Plastigauge before final assembly.
verification: Journal-clearance readings recorded and measuring material removed.

steps.title: Resolve cam and chain defects
steps.instruction: If journal clearance failed, measure journal OD against 22.002–22.015 mm: a failed journal requires a cam, while an in-range journal with failed clearance requires head and caps together. Inspect chain for stiffness/damage and sprockets for more than one-quarter tooth wear; either condition requires chain and cam replacement as a set. Check smooth decompressor movement and projecting lever pin. Cross-check the recorded lower-chain inspection and installed crank/chain against the cams selected here. Any required matched crank-sprocket/chain/cam set must now be complete and individually accepted; do not retain old cams when matched-set renewal is required. The head/cap-set replacement remains outside this route.
verification: Cam, chain, sprocket and decompressor disposition accepted.
steps.composition_adaptation: Explicit combined lower/top-end component state and exact OEM break-in groups; source mechanics retained.

steps.title: Install the rings
steps.instruction: Install the oil expander, lower rail, upper rail, second ring and top ring in that order. Manufacturer marks or numbers face upward. Use the accepted matched parts from the measurement records.
verification: Ring order and markings confirmed.

steps.title: Fit piston, pin and new clips
steps.instruction: Oil the piston and pin with engine oil. Orient the piston mark toward the exhaust/rear of the engine. Protect the case opening while inserting pin and new clips. Fully seat the clips, keeping each clip end away from the piston cutout.
verification: Orientation and new clip seating confirmed.

steps.title: Set the ring-gap positions
steps.instruction: Oil piston, rings and cylinder. Match the five end-gap positions exactly to this diagram, including its 15° offsets: a top ring, b second ring, c upper oil rail, d expander, e lower oil rail. Use the piston drawing as the orientation reference rather than guessing clock positions.
verification: Five ring-gap positions checked against the diagram.

steps.title: Install the cylinder
steps.instruction: Account for and remove the crankcase protective cloth before lowering the cylinder, keeping the timing chain supported. Install new base gasket and dowels. Compress the rings by hand as the cylinder is lowered, passing the timing chain and exhaust-side guide through their cavity. Do not force a snagged ring. Tighten the cylinder bolt to 10 N·m.
verification: Cylinder seated without ring damage; bolt tightened.

steps.title: Seat the accepted head
steps.instruction: Confirm final piston fit, valve/head checks and selected repair are accepted. Install intake-side guide, dowels, new head gasket and head while drawing the chain upward. Match the gasket orientation to the illustration and keep passages clear.
verification: Head and new gasket correctly seated; chain retained.

steps.title: Prepare the main head bolts
steps.instruction: Wash bolt threads/contact surfaces, both washer contact faces, head contact faces and crankcase threads. Apply molybdenum disulfide grease to the four main-bolt threads/contact faces and both washer faces. Install washers and bolts, lightly seating them in the installation diagram order. Keep the small bolts distinct.
verification: Four main bolts and washers prepared as specified.

steps.title: Tighten the first stage
steps.instruction: Following installation diagram order 1–4, tighten the main bolts to 36 N·m in two or three stages. Do not use the removal-diagram numbering.
verification: First 36 N·m stage and order recorded.

steps.title: Retighten one main bolt at a time
steps.instruction: Remove only installation bolt 1, without loosening any other. Reapply molybdenum disulfide grease to threads/contact face and both washer faces. Refit at 18 N·m, make reference marks and turn an additional 90°. Complete the same entire operation on bolts 2, 3 and 4 individually in order; finish each before loosening the next.
verification: Each individual 18 N·m plus 90° stage recorded.

steps.title: Finish the head fastening
steps.instruction: In installation order 1–4 turn each main bolt a further 60°. Apply LOCTITE locking agent to the two small bolts and tighten installation positions 5 and 6 to 12 N·m. Keep molybdenum grease preparation and locking-agent preparation separate.
verification: Final 60° stages and small-bolt 12 N·m recorded.

steps.title: Set the cams at TDC
steps.instruction: Account for and remove all protective cloths from the head and timing-chain space before installing the cams. Turn the crank counterclockwise to align rotor TDC with the cover mark. Apply molybdenum disulfide oil to cams and engine oil to the decompressor. Fit chain onto both sprockets and set both cam marks at the cap-surface edges in the diagram. Do not rotate the crank while installing cams.
verification: Rotor/cam alignment recorded.

steps.title: Secure the cam caps
steps.instruction: Install the matching caps and dowels. Oil cap-bolt threads and contact surfaces. Tighten evenly to 10 N·m in two or three stages following the exact eight-bolt sequence shown; no forced or uneven seating.
verification: Caps seated and exact sequence/torque recorded.

steps.title: Fit and release the tensioner
steps.instruction: Wind the rod fully clockwise with light finger pressure. Fit new illustrated body/sealing gaskets, tensioner UP mark upward, and mounting bolts at 10 N·m. Release the screwdriver and confirm smooth rod extension, then install the new cap gasket and cap bolt at 6 N·m.
verification: Tensioner extended smoothly; gaskets and 10/6 N·m settings confirmed.

steps.title: Check timing by hand
steps.instruction: Turn the crank counterclockwise several turns without forcing resistance. Return rotor TDC to the cover mark and verify both cam marks match the head/cap surfaces. Correct any mismatch before proceeding; never use the starter to test unresolved timing.
verification: Several-turn hand check and all timing marks accepted.

steps.title: Measure the final cold clearances
steps.instruction: At the confirmed TDC position and room temperature, record all four gaps using a feeler gauge. Intake 0.10–0.17 mm; exhaust 0.15–0.22 mm. Choose the next action from the actual readings; these results do not automatically approve closure.
verification: Four readings and required next action recorded.

steps.title: Choose adjustment or closure
steps.instruction: If all four cold readings are within specification, choose the close-up branch. Otherwise continue with the pad adjustment below using the actual current installed pad and measured gap. Unsupported pad selection or a component fault cannot be bypassed by selecting close-up.
verification: Reading-based path recorded.

branches.label: All four cold clearances pass — close the engine
branches.condition: All four latest cold readings are in range and all timing checks pass; no adjustment required.

steps.title: Reopen the cam and pad access
steps.instruction: At the confirmed TDC position remove tensioner cap, mounting bolts and tensioner. Loosen cap bolts evenly crisscross from outside inward, lift matching caps/cams and secure the chain. Lift each affected lifter/pad with the lapper, protecting the opening and preserving exact positions.
verification: Cams and affected pads removed without losing identity or chain position.

steps.title: Select each replacement pad from the correct chart
steps.instruction: Record the current installed pad number. Convert its last digit only as listed: 0/1/2 to 0; 4/5/6 to 5; 8/9 to the next ten (148 becomes 150). Digits 3 and 7 are unspecified. Use the intake chart or exhaust chart to intersect the measured cold-gap row with that pad column. Record the resulting pad number. Blank cells, unreadable numbers, unlisted digit conversions or readings between/outside chart rows require clarification, not extrapolation. Available stock pads are 1.20–2.40 mm in 0.05 mm increments.
verification: Each new pad traced to exact valve, current pad and chart cell.

steps.title: Install the selected pads
steps.instruction: Apply molybdenum disulfide oil to stem ends and engine oil to lifters. Fit correct selected pads with numbers up and original lifters in their original positions. Do not twist them forcibly; each lifter must rotate smoothly with a finger. After securing every pad and lifter, account for and remove the protective cloth from the timing-chain space before the next cam-installation step.
verification: Selected pads installed in recorded positions.

steps.title: Set the cams at TDC
steps.instruction: Turn the crank counterclockwise to align rotor TDC with the cover mark. Apply molybdenum disulfide oil to cams and engine oil to the decompressor. Fit chain onto both sprockets and set both cam marks at the cap-surface edges in the diagram. Do not rotate the crank while installing cams.
verification: Rotor/cam alignment recorded.

steps.title: Secure the cam caps
steps.instruction: Install the matching caps and dowels. Oil cap-bolt threads and contact surfaces. Tighten evenly to 10 N·m in two or three stages following the exact eight-bolt sequence shown; no forced or uneven seating.
verification: Caps seated and exact sequence/torque recorded.

steps.title: Fit and release the tensioner
steps.instruction: Wind the rod fully clockwise with light finger pressure. Fit new illustrated body/sealing gaskets, tensioner UP mark upward, and mounting bolts at 10 N·m. Release the screwdriver and confirm smooth rod extension, then install the new cap gasket and cap bolt at 6 N·m.
verification: Tensioner extended smoothly; gaskets and 10/6 N·m settings confirmed.

steps.title: Check timing by hand
steps.instruction: Turn the crank counterclockwise several turns without forcing resistance. Return rotor TDC to the cover mark and verify both cam marks match the head/cap surfaces. Correct any mismatch before proceeding; never use the starter to test unresolved timing.
verification: Several-turn hand check and all timing marks accepted.

steps.title: Measure the final cold clearances
steps.instruction: At the confirmed TDC position and room temperature, record all four gaps using a feeler gauge. Intake 0.10–0.17 mm; exhaust 0.15–0.22 mm. Choose the next action from the actual readings; these results do not automatically approve closure.
verification: Four readings and required next action recorded.

steps.title: Accept the adjusted clearances
steps.instruction: All four latest readings must now be within the cold specifications. If any fail, repeat the cam-removal, chart selection, installation, timing and measurement sequence before marking this step complete. Preserve every changed pad and final reading in the record; do not continue to the cover with failed clearance.
verification: All four final cold readings and timing accepted.

steps.title: Reseal the head cover
steps.instruction: Fit the top chain guide, new head-cover gasket and new plug-hole gasket. Apply ThreeBond 1541C to the cover gasket as illustrated, install the cover and tighten its bolts to 10 N·m. Keep the retained breather plate intact.
verification: Guide and new gaskets seated; cover secured.

steps.title: Close plug and timing access
steps.instruction: Restore the head breather. Clean the spark plug and its gasket seat, install at 13 N·m and refit the cap when its engine interface is restored. Fit two new access-screw O-rings with lithium-soap-based grease, oil the screw threads, and tighten timing-mark screw to 6 N·m and crankshaft-end screw to 10 N·m.
verification: Plug, breather and both access ports closed with correct preparation.

steps.title: Accept the completed top-end work before engine refit
steps.instruction: Record the actual completed lower-engine and top-end work: installed crank/chain/cam matched-set disposition, gear/shaft and case-bearing measurements, lower-drive/clutch torques and free movement, piston/cylinder/ring and valve/guide measurements, any completed specialist seat work, accepted cold valve clearances, timing, lubrication and free rotation. Confirm the top-end covers, access plugs and renewed oil-filter closure are sealed before refit; no unresolved bench fault may pass this handoff. Keep the original swingarm and side stacks located on their temporary support for the single pivot replacement.
verification: Actual lower/top-end parts, measurements, matched timing components and cold timing accepted; all covers/filter sealed; original swingarm side stacks supported.
steps.composition_adaptation: Explicit combined lower/top-end component state and exact OEM break-in groups; source mechanics retained.

steps.title: Place the engine back in the chassis
steps.instruction: Bring the supported engine in from the right, lower part first, and align mounting points without trapping wires or hoses. Apply molybdenum-disulfide grease to the pivot and install from the right while withdrawing the temporary support shaft, keeping the original swingarm side stacks located. Apply lithium-soap grease to the pivot-nut threads and contact face.
verification: Engine aligned from right; pivot from right; supports and grease correct.

steps.title: Install and secure the engine brackets
steps.instruction: Restore the original lower and upper brackets and mapped hardware. Follow the labeled engine-install drawing: pivot nut 75 N·m; lower engine-mount bolt 53 N·m; front bracket bolts 34 N·m; front engine-mount bolt 55 N·m; upper bracket bolts 34 N·m; upper engine-mount bolts 45 N·m. Keep the supported assembly aligned while tightening.
verification: All six distinct mounting torque groups recorded against the diagram.

steps.title: Reconnect and adjust the cable clutch
steps.instruction: Restore the identified clutch cable outer to its engine bracket and nipple to the push lever as illustrated; tighten the engine-end cable locknut to 7 Nm if loosened. Verify full seating. Set lever free play to 7-12 mm using the handlebar adjuster first. If its range is insufficient, slide the cable cover, loosen the cable-side adjuster locknut, adjust and tighten that locknut to 4.3 Nm, then restore the cover. Check smooth clutch operation through both steering locks and record actual free play.
verification: Engine cable-end and outer fully seated; disturbed engine locknut 7 Nm; cable-side adjuster locknut 4.3 Nm if used; actual lever free play 7-12 mm recorded.

steps.title: Restore pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Install new matching pedal-pivot O-rings at the two illustrated positions, lubricated with lithium-soap grease. Restore the brake-pedal pivot and spring, lubricating illustrated pivot/seal contacts with lithium-soap grease; tighten its bolt to 26 Nm. Refit the engine guard at 7 Nm. Restore the head breather to its recorded case/engine connections and exact top-view route. Keep ignition, ground and temperature leads outside the breather and avoid pinching under case brackets.
verification: Pedal 26/guard 7 N·m; spring attached; breather routing and marks correct.

steps.title: Restore the drive sprocket and chain
steps.instruction: Fit the original serviceable drive sprocket and new correct lock washer. Leave the nut hand-threaded temporarily; its final LOCTITE preparation, torque and tab locking are a later explicit step after rear-wheel, brake and chain closure. Align shift-shaft/pedal punch marks and tighten the pedal bolt to 12 Nm. With the supported rear wheel still installed, loosen the axle nut and both adjuster locknuts and back off adjusters enough to bring the wheel forward for chain installation. Fit the retained stock chain with matched link/plate and new clip, closed end leading chain travel as illustrated; lubricate the chain. Leave the sprocket cover off for the final nut check.
verification: Original sprocket and new lock washer seated; nut temporary only; new chain clip correctly oriented; shift pedal 12 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the engine ground and starter lead
steps.instruction: Refit the ground terminal at the cylinder-head location shown and tighten its bolt 7 N·m; point the lead upward and route it outside the high-tension cord. Refit the starter lead at 6 N·m while holding the motor-side nut with a spanner. Restore its clamp without slack, as shown.
verification: Head ground 7 N·m and upward; starter 6 N·m with terminal counterheld.

steps.title: Reconnect and route the engine harness
steps.instruction: Reconnect stator, crankshaft-position, gear-position and coolant-temperature connectors and their covers. Route stator lead behind the radiator, clear of the tension arm and gear-position connector. The clutch CABLE protector contacts the radiator hose and passes outside the stator and gear leads. Restore the lower tie between the illustrated left-cover bolts with lock OUTWARD, and upper tie over the grommet with lock FORWARD. Clamp the clutch cable ahead of the lead and seat the frame clip with lock forward. Keep regulator leads inside the tension arm. Fully seat the plug cap and route temperature, engine-ground and high-tension leads outside the head breather. Check the starter lead stays clear of the push lever shaft.
verification: Every labeled connector latched/covered; source routing and tie locations verified.

steps.title: Reseat the throttle body
steps.instruction: Remove intake protection and seat the intact throttle body fully in its original engine-side joint. Restore the clamp orientation and tighten the throttle-body joint clamp to 3.0 N·m. Keep both cables routed without tension and check full smooth throttle return. Sensors and calibration screws remain untouched.
verification: Joint fully seated 3.0 N·m; throttle returns smoothly; cables not trapped.

steps.title: Lubricate the sliding and cable-end surfaces
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the throttle-grip sliding surface. Lightly grease the cable ends and inside of the grip as shown. Keep grease away from the exterior gripping surface and the brake.
verification: Sliding and cable-end contact surfaces lubricated.

steps.title: Reconnect pull and return cables
steps.instruction: Restore each identified cable end to its original seat and groove in the throttle tube. Place the rubber cover and slide the intact grip/tube onto the handlebar. Confirm both cable ends and their outer housings are seated correctly before closing the housing.
verification: Both cable ends seated in the correct positions without crossing.

steps.title: Secure the housing
steps.instruction: Fit the housing and tighten its screws to 3.8 Nm. Check grip movement immediately. If the housing causes binding, reposition and retighten it, then check again. Restore the housing cover and rubber cover.
verification: Housing torqued; grip moves smoothly and returns.

steps.title: Verify free play and return before starting
steps.instruction: With the engine stopped, check free play and smooth full return through the steering travel. The retained setup must still have 3–6 mm free play and no binding. If not, correct seating/routing before starting; do not use a running engine to diagnose a bound throttle.
verification: Record 3–6 mm free play and full return at centre and both steering limits.

steps.title: Reconnect the engine coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Remove temporary port covers. Restore radiator hoses 1,3 and 4 to their marked engine connections and original clamp positions; tighten each disturbed radiator-hose clamp screw to 1.5 N·m. Check there are no kinks or trapped hoses. Radiator pipe seals and temperature sensor were not removed.
verification: Hoses 1/3/4 correct; disturbed clamps 1.5 N·m.

steps.title: Seat the new header gasket
steps.instruction: Install the new exhaust-port gasket at the cylinder head and refit header pipe 1. Tighten all header nuts first to 7 N·m, then retighten them to 10 N·m. Do not apply the protector-screw locking-agent note to these nuts.
verification: New exhaust-port gasket; all header nuts 7 then 10 Nm.

steps.title: Locate pipe 2 and its clamp
steps.instruction: Install the new pipe-joint gaskets in their PDF202 positions. Refit the pipe-2 clamp, pipe 2 and bracket bolt. At each joint, engage the clamp projection in the pipe/silencer slot and keep the clamp off the raised projection illustrated in PDF208. Leave final bracket and clamp tightening until the silencer is seated.
verification: Fresh joint seals seated; clamp locating features correct.

steps.title: Refit the complete silencer
steps.instruction: Refit the silencer clamp and complete silencer on the seated joint. Install the retained mounting hardware and tighten both silencer mounting bolts to 30 N·m.
verification: Both silencer mounts 30 N·m; joints fully engaged.

steps.title: Tighten the bracket and both clamps
