steps.instruction: Confirm front and rear joints remain fully inserted while tightening the exhaust-pipe bracket bolt to 20 N·m, pipe-2 clamp bolt to 16 N·m and silencer clamp bolt to 16 N·m.
verification: Bracket 20 N·m; each joint clamp 16 N·m; projections correctly located.

steps.title: Seat the case and secure its mounts
steps.instruction: Remove temporary inlet protection and seat the complete case fully on its original intake connection. Restore mounting collars, dampers and washers; tighten the three case bolts to 7 Nm and the air-filter-case joint clamp screw to 3 Nm. Restore the cylinder-head breather connection to the case if released and its original spring clamp. Check the lip is evenly seated, reconnect the intake-temperature coupler and restore its cover.
verification: Three mounts 7 N·m; joint clamp 3 N·m; joint fully seated; sensor connector latched.

steps.title: Verify the restored intake
steps.instruction: Check case support, full joint seating, wiring clearance and that all temporary intake protection has been removed. The filter and bracket stayed assembled; if either has moved or a seal cannot be accounted for, resolve it before closing the bike.
verification: Intake complete and clean; retained assembly bracket/element secure.

steps.title: Reconnect the fuel system
steps.instruction: Refit the tank on its retained dampers/collars. Tighten its two front mounting bolts to 8 N·m and the tank retaining screw to 4 N·m. Remove the temporary joint covers, push the fuel hose fully onto the pipe until it clicks, and slide the connector cover back into its locked position. Keep the hose holder correctly oriented, with no kink or pinch. Reconnect the pump plug.
verification: Tank front bolts 8 N·m/retaining screw 4 N·m; hose latched/covered/routed; pump plug connected.

steps.title: Refill with the specified mixture
steps.instruction: Use the specified aluminum-compatible ethylene-glycol antifreeze and distilled water at a final 1:1 coolant-to-water ratio. Do not mix antifreeze types. Fill to the maximum level illustrated in PDF104. The complete system nominal volume is 1.03 L including all routes; correct level and concentration govern, not forcing in that amount after an incomplete drain. Wash any spill on paint away immediately with water.
verification: Mixture/product and amount recorded; level at illustrated maximum.

steps.title: Secure the radiator cap
steps.instruction: Install and secure the radiator cap. Account for the drain hardware, collection container and tools before running the engine.
verification: Cap secured; drain sealed; tools clear.

steps.title: Refill the oil for the actual engine condition
steps.instruction: This route split the crankcases and reassembled the engine: measure the OEM disassembled-engine quantity of 1.20 L for this initial fill. The later post-break-in filter/oil change uses its own 0.96 L service quantity. Use the OEM-listed Yamalube/API SG-or-higher JASO MA oil from the listed SAE grades 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50. Do not add chemical additives or use source-excluded energy-conserving oils. Record chosen product and quantity; no temperature-to-grade chart is asserted by these pages. Lubricate the new filler-cap O-ring with lithium-soap grease as shown in exact OEM PDF246, then fit the cap. Final level and flow checks remain required.
verification: Disassembled-engine initial 1.20 L fill, oil grade and new greased filler O-ring recorded; subsequent flow and settled-level verification still required.
steps.composition_adaptation: Explicit combined lower/top-end component state and exact OEM break-in groups; source mechanics retained.

steps.title: Reconnect the battery and inspect routing
steps.instruction: Recheck all engine interfaces, then reconnect positive battery lead before negative. Restore positive-terminal cover and the exact illustrated lead routing, with positive lead below negative. Keep all loose conductors away from the frame and secure the original connections.
verification: Positive then negative restored; terminal cover/routing correct.

steps.title: Refit the panels and seat
steps.instruction: Locate the radiator-guard projections in the shroud holes, then install the shrouds at 7 N·m. Refit the air-filter-case cover by engaging its projection and both ribs. Slide side-cover tabs into their slots; the right-cover rib sits under the rear-fender rib. Tighten ordinary left/right side-cover bolts to 7 N·m and the two seat bolts to 13 N·m. Refit the sub-seat with its tether untwisted, then press, rotate and secure its quick fastener.
verification: Tabs/ribs seated; shrouds/side-cover bolts 7 N·m; seat bolts 13 N·m; quick fastener locked.

steps.title: Measure and adjust chain slack
steps.instruction: Loosen the rear axle nut and both adjuster locknuts first. With the rear wheel raised and gearbox in neutral, pull the chain upward above the chain-guide mounting bolt with about 50 N. Measure between the drive-chain guide and the bottom of the chain at the exact diagram location. Adjust both sides equally to 50–60 mm. Push the wheel forward so each puller/end plate is seated against the swingarm end.
verification: Measured slack 50–60 mm using OEM50 N reference; pullers equally adjusted and seated.

steps.title: Secure the rear axle and adjusters
steps.instruction: Tighten the rear axle nut to 135 N·m and both chain-adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m. Recheck the chain slack after tightening.
verification: Axle 135 N·m; locknuts 21 N·m; final slack recorded.

steps.title: Lock the drive sprocket after rear-wheel closure
steps.instruction: With the rear axle and adjusters torqued, chain fitted and rear brake refitted and firm, keep the transmission in neutral and have a helper apply the rear brake to hold the drive. Remove the temporarily fitted nut, apply Yamaha-specified LOCTITE to its threads and tighten to 90 Nm with a torque wrench. Record the actual locking product and follow its instructions; Yamaha does not name a grade here. Bend the new washer tabs against the nut flats, inspect locking and fit the sprocket cover at 7 Nm. No impact or heat is part of this method.
verification: Rear wheel, chain and working brake restored before holding load; nut 90 Nm with specified locking agent; new tab washer locked; cover 7 Nm.

steps.title: Accept the completed repair
steps.instruction: Record the actual lower-engine and top-end parts installed and all accepted cold timing, clearance, fit and refit records from this route. The bike remains fully cool and has not yet been started after repair. Complete the following filter/static checks and pressure-tester attachment before its first oil-flow start. Any unresolved mechanical or lubrication-preparation fault remains open.
verification: Actual repair records accepted; engine fully cool; first startup has not occurred.
steps.composition_adaptation: Explicit combined lower/top-end component state and exact OEM break-in groups; source mechanics retained.

steps.title: Choose the actual parts route
steps.instruction: Record all replaced parts. A new cylinder or complete crankshaft requires about one hour: 20 minutes at no more than half throttle, inspect, then 40 minutes at no more than three-quarter throttle and inspect again. New valves, piston, rings, camshaft or gears require about 30 minutes at no more than half throttle. With both groups renewed, retain half throttle for the first 30 minutes; this overlap is an explicit conservative workflow adaptation. No riding proceeds with unresolved lower or top-end faults.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.
steps.composition_adaptation: Explicit combined lower/top-end component state and exact OEM break-in groups; source mechanics retained.

steps.title: Open filter access
steps.instruction: Release the sub-seat quick fastener. Press the intake-duct side inward, release both cover ribs, lift its rear and slide rearward out of the front projection. Release the retaining band and move the bracket in the arrow direction shown in the diagram. Withdraw filter/guide together and separate the filter, guide and seal. Leave the bracket mounted.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Clean and oil the foam
steps.instruction: Wash with air-filter cleaner or kerosene, squeeze without twisting and dry fully. Replace damaged foam. Work Yamaha or quality foam-filter oil evenly through the foam in a bag; wipe excess with a clean cloth. It must be wet throughout but not dripping. Do not use gasoline or the source-prohibited volatile cleaners.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Restore the sealed intake
steps.instruction: Fit seal/filter to the guide and grease the entire seal lips with lithium-soap grease. Move the bracket rearward, engage the guide projection with it and secure the other projection in the band. Engage cover projection and both ribs. Restore the breather through guide/groove, protected end in steering shaft and other end on cap. Secure sub-seat with tether untwisted.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Perform the pre-ride inspection
steps.instruction: Complete the pre-ride inspection: coolant/fuel/oil levels and no leaks; sequential shifts and smooth clutch; effective brakes; full throttle return and 3–6 mm free play; aligned lubricated chain; wheels/spokes/tires; smooth steering without play; smooth leak-free suspension; unrestricted cables and secure connectors. Cold tire pressure is 100 kPa (15 psi) front/rear. Correct failures before riding.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Restore fuel and verify readiness to start
steps.instruction: Open the sub-seat access and add clean recommended unleaded gasoline, minimum 91 (R+M)/2; E10 is permitted. Secure the fuel cap and sub-seat fastener with its tether untwisted. Check the pump connector and latched fuel hose/cover, and check for fuel leaks. Select neutral and work in a ventilated area before any starter operation.
verification: Correct fuel restored; cap/fastener secured; hose/connector checked; no fuel leak; neutral selected.

steps.title: Attach the pressure tester while cold
steps.instruction: Use the Mityvac MV4560 method only with confirmed correct radiator adapter fit. With the engine fully cool, remove the cap under a thick cloth, slowly vent at the detent, then remove after hissing stops. Fill coolant to the source upper level and inspect hoses. Wet the adapter seal with water or coolant, seat it in the filler neck and secure both hose compression connections. Keep the original cap off until testing and full cooling are finished.
verification: Record the actual equipment, condition and test result; unresolved faults remain pending.

steps.title: Verify oil flow immediately at idle
steps.instruction: With fuel, intake, electrical and mounting closure complete and the correctly fitting cold-installed pressure tester connected as just checked, start the engine at idle only. Observe the oil window for flow and decreasing level while monitoring the pressure gauge. If oil level does not decrease, or pressure rises rapidly toward the stated ceiling, stop immediately; do not rev to force oil flow. The following three-minute warm-up is continuous with this initial idle start.
verification: Oil flow/level decrease observed at idle; no leak or abnormal condition.

steps.title: Warm with the gauge connected
steps.instruction: Monitor the connected gauge while warming for Yamaha’s three minutes. Stop for rapid pressure rise, abnormal gauge behavior, leaks or pressure approaching the 137.3 kPa ceiling. Do not pump above that ceiling. If stopped for a fault, let the system cool fully before releasing pressure or disconnecting; investigate before repeating. This sequence combines Mityvac cold attachment/engine-on monitoring with Yamaha’s head-gasket warm-up requirement.
verification: Record the actual equipment, condition and test result; unresolved faults remain pending.

steps.title: Check cooling-system pressure
steps.instruction: After the three-minute warm-up, stop the engine and apply only enough pressure to reach 137.3 kPa (19.9 psi), never exceed it. Confirm it holds for 5–10 seconds. Check radiator/hose joints for leakage and hoses for bulging. A loss of pressure or visible defect requires correction and repeat testing; record actual pressure and hold time.
verification: Record the actual equipment, condition and test result; unresolved faults remain pending.

steps.title: Cool fully before removing the tester
steps.instruction: Leave the connected equipment undisturbed until the engine is completely cool. Then use the MV4560 relief lever to release remaining pressure before disconnecting under a cloth. Refill to the source level and refit the radiator cap. This cold-release restriction comes from Mityvac page9; never remove a hot cap or hot pressurized adapter.
verification: Record the actual equipment, condition and test result; unresolved faults remain pending.

steps.title: Warm for the operating checks
steps.instruction: After the pressure-test equipment has been removed cold, coolant restored and the radiator cap secured, restart the engine and warm it for the following measured operating checks. Keep the cap closed and watch for oil flow, leaks or abnormal noise; stop immediately for a fault.
verification: Initial oil flow verified; engine warmed for the next measured operating checks; cap remains closed.

steps.title: Check the warm idle
steps.instruction: Use the correctly configured YDT 90890-03275 (US USB) or 90890-03273 to confirm coolant at 70–80 °C. Measure speed with tachometer 90890-06760 or YU-39951-B, connected as shown to the ignition-coil high-tension lead. With the starter knob fully returned and normal filter/compression/free play, verify 1900–2100 r/min. If necessary, adjust the idle screw; clockwise raises speed.
verification: Record temperature and accepted idle speed.

steps.title: Set the final grip free play
steps.instruction: Stop the engine. If final adjustment is needed after idle setting, loosen the grip adjuster locknut, turn the adjuster to obtain 3–6 mm free play, and tighten the locknut. Confirm smooth full return again.
verification: Record final 3–6 mm free play and secure locknut.

steps.title: Verify idle through steering travel
steps.instruction: Restart the warm engine without starter enrichment. Turn the handlebar fully left and right: idle must not change. If it changes, stop and correct cable routing/seating or adjustment before repeating this check. Hold the engine-stop switch until the engine fully stops when the check is finished.
verification: Record unchanged idle across steering travel; engine stopped.

steps.title: Allow complete cooling
steps.instruction: After the operating check has stopped the engine, let it cool completely before opening the radiator cap for the next cold-level check.
verification: Engine stopped and fully cooled before the cap is opened.

steps.title: Recheck the cold level
steps.instruction: Keep the bike upright on level ground. With the engine cooled, use the cloth and slow pressure-release method to remove the cap. Allow the coolant to settle, check against the illustrated maximum and add the correct mixture if low. Restore the cap securely. A leak or repeatedly dropping level requires repair rather than repeated top-offs.
verification: Final cold level and mixture recorded; cap secured; no unresolved loss.

steps.title: Verify the installed engine and record closure
steps.instruction: Follow the oil-level procedure with the bike upright: warm the engine for ten minutes to the stated normal oil temperature of 60 C, stop, stand upright on level ground, then restart for 10 seconds, stop and allow a few minutes to settle. Level must be between the window lower edge and maximum mark. Correct level with the recommended oil; warm for several minutes and recheck after settling as directed. Check leaks, cable-clutch free play 7-12 mm and brake operation, throttle free play 3-6 mm/full return, and the recorded warm-idle steering test. Record mount torques, fluid quantities, chain slack and unresolved symptoms. Engine installation completion does not substitute for an internal rebuild record. Verify wheels remain correctly secured, brakes firm, no trapped cable/hose, and all temporary supports and port covers removed. Record any fault before returning the bike to use.
verification: Oil level/flow, coolant level, leak/control checks and hardware record complete.

steps.title: Ride the first interval
steps.instruction: Warm the fully assembled engine using its accepted starting procedure. In a controlled off-road area, ride about20 minutes at no more than half throttle. Stop immediately for a problem and record actual riding time/symptoms. Automatic stop after7 minutes idling does not make idling into riding time.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Stop and inspect
steps.instruction: Check mounted areas for looseness and oil or other leaks. Resolve any problem before continuing. Record actual findings; a symptom-free interval does not complete post-break-in maintenance.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Complete the recorded parts route
steps.instruction: For valves/piston/rings/camshaft/gears without cylinder or crankshaft replacement, ride about 10 further minutes at no more than half throttle. For a new cylinder or crankshaft, ride about 40 further minutes; with any 30-minute-group parts renewed too, retain half throttle for the first 10 minutes of this second session, then never exceed three-quarter throttle. Stop for abnormal behavior and record actual time, throttle ceiling and symptoms.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Inspect before maintenance
steps.instruction: Stop and thoroughly inspect mounted areas and leakage, cable stretch, brake action/free play, chain stretch and loose spokes. The riding period is complete only for the recorded parts route; maintenance below remains unfinished.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Drain and inspect the used oil
steps.instruction: Upright on level ground, warm the engine several minutes and stop. Place a clean container under both drains. Remove filler cap/O-ring and crankcase/oil-tank drain bolts with gaskets; drain both compartments completely. Inspect for dirt and foreign material, especially metal chips. If present, stop: Yamaha requires crankcase disassembly/inspection, not merely fresh oil and a passed record.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Renew the oil filter
steps.instruction: Renew the oil filter during this oil change. Remove the cover and old filter. Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the new cover O-ring, install it, and fit the exact new filter in the diagram orientation. Refit the cover bolts at 10 N·m. Filter renewal is included in this route; the post-break-in list itself requires the oil change.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Expose the generator mounting check
steps.instruction: With oil drained, remove sub-seat/seat, filter-case cover and left shroud. Label/disconnect stator and crank-position couplers. Remove the shift pedal, preserving punch-mark alignment, and retain both external lead clamps/holder. Keep the engine installed during this inspection.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Open the left cover only
steps.instruction: Release cover fasteners progressively and lift the cover without pulling wires. Retain both dowels and holders/clamps; discard the gasket. Keep stator/grommet attached to the cover and rotor attached to the shaft. Secure assemblies do not need removal merely for a mounting inspection.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Inspect generator mounting
steps.instruction: Check generator rotor and stator mounted areas for looseness and visible contact damage, and inspect connectors. Keep sound mounted assemblies intact. Record the actual inspection. Loose or damaged assemblies require separate generator repair with correct taper/key, sealing and fastening steps; a blind torque check does not replace that repair.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Reseal the left side
steps.instruction: Fit both dowels and a new cover gasket. Restore cover/holders/clamps and tighten bolts in stages and crisscross to10Nm. Keep the undisturbed grommet sealed and wires unpinched. Align pedal/shaft punch marks, tighten the pedal bolt to 12 N·m, reconnect both couplers and restore the illustrated lead routing.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Close drains and refill
steps.instruction: Fit new drain gaskets: oil-tank bolt 10 N·m, crankcase bolt 20 N·m. Fill 0.96 L for this filter-removal service and install filler cap with a new O-ring. Use Yamalube or an oil meeting API SG or higher and JASO MA; the listed SAE grades are 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50. Do not add additives or use the source-prohibited CD-or-higher or ENERGY CONSERVING II oils. The settled window level is the final check. The 1.20 L disassembled capacity is not this service refill. Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the new filler-cap O-ring as shown in the engine-cover diagram.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Inspect the repaired engine
steps.instruction: Check head/cylinder and crankcase/cover joints for pressure/oil leaks and cooling-system leakage. Check silencer body/stay for cracks/leaks and engine mounts for loosening. Record the actual repaired-part fit and contact inspection with the repair specialist where needed. Accepted old dimensions alone are not a fresh inspection of inaccessible surfaces; any suspect fit must be resolved before completion.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Inspect chassis and wheels
steps.instruction: Check frame, swingarm, linkage and bracket welds/mounts for cracks/looseness; wheels for damage/runout and bearing play. A tilted tire valve indicates tire movement requiring correction. Check fork/shock smooth operation, leaks and mounts. Raise front wheel, rock lower fork legs to check steering play and turn both ways; binding/play needs separate steering service.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Check spokes progressively
steps.instruction: Compare spoke tones by tapping: loose spokes sound dull. Replace bent/damaged spokes through the separate wheel repair. Tighten sound loose nipples progressively to 2.5 N·m, never a half-turn or more per adjustment. Continue staged checks until initial looseness disappears; record unresolved wheel faults.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Set chain alignment and slack
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel raised and transmission neutral, pull up the chain about 50 N above the guide mounting bolt and measure the illustrated guide-to-chain gap: 50–60 mm. To adjust, loosen axle nut and both locknuts; adjust sides equally and push wheel forward to seat both end plates. Tighten axle 135 N·m and locknuts 21 N·m, then recheck alignment/slack. Lubricate the chain. A stiff, damaged or worn chain requires separate cleaning/removal or replacement and clip closure; do not hide that work behind this inspection.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Inspect and lubricate controls
steps.instruction: Check both brakes for effective action without drag and the front-lever end for no free play. With reservoirs horizontal, fluid must be above the minimum marks in the diagram. Leaks or spongy action require separate brake service. Check cable-clutch free play at 7.0–12.0 mm: turn the handlebar adjuster; if insufficient, slide the cable cover, loosen its locknut, adjust at the cable, tighten that locknut to 4.3 N·m and restore the cover. Check smooth clutch action and unrestricted cable travel through full steering. Replace damaged cables; lubricate rough sound cables with engine oil or suitable cable lubricant at the upright cable end. Use silicone grease at brake-lever moving contacts and lithium-soap grease at clutch-lever and pedal pivots.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Record the required tank-interior service
steps.instruction: The post-break-in list requires cleaning inside the fuel tank and checking for leaks. Record actual qualified cleaning, not merely an appointment or fuel-color inspection. The cleaning method remains an external dependency. Follow exact tank access/refit: extract fuel with a pump; remove seat, side covers and shrouds; cover residual-pressure fittings with cloth, release holder/cover and both connector buttons by hand, protect disconnected joints and support the tank off its pump face. If pump removed, renew gasket lip upward, align pump projection with bracket slot and tighten the five bolts in the numbered order to 7 N·m. Restore tank front bolts 8 N·m and retaining screw 4 N·m, reconnect fuel hose until it clicks, restore connector cover and correctly oriented holder, and connect pump coupler. Record restored sealing and leak checks.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Restore access panels
steps.instruction: Seat the radiator-guard projections in the left shroud and tighten shroud fasteners to 7 N·m. Restore filter-cover projections/ribs and breather routing. Refit seat bolts to 13 N·m and secure the sub-seat with untwisted tether. Restore any other bodywork removed for tank cleaning using its exact diagram. Confirm all connectors, wire clearance, fuel connections and oil closures before restart.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Complete every applicable torque check
steps.instruction: Complete the post-break-in fastener checks using the linked joint table and its preparation conditions: frame/engine/seat, steering, suspension/linkage/pivot, wheels/spokes/sprocket, brake/clutch fasteners, fuel pump, shift pedal and bodywork. Record each joint or link the actual inspection sheet. Inaccessible/unidentified joints remain pending. Do not substitute generic torques or open hydraulic unions merely to create a check. Lower steering-ring preload requires its separate staged service. No completion with unresolved required checks.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Check flow at idle
steps.instruction: Start fully assembled engine at idle only and watch oil window for flow and decreasing level. Stop immediately if level does not decrease; diagnose lubrication before proceeding. Do not rev it to force a successful check.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Verify settled oil level
steps.instruction: Warm the oil to the specified normal 60°C (source says ten minutes; automatic idle stop may interrupt), stop, stand upright/level, run ten seconds, stop and wait a few minutes. Level must lie between lower window edge and maximum mark. Correct with specified oil, then warm several minutes, stop, settle and recheck. Record actual level/leaks; do not claim an unmeasured temperature was measured.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Record actual maintenance completion
steps.instruction: After the engine is fully cool, check coolant at the illustrated maximum and confirm no continuing loss. Open a radiator cap only cold, using a thick cloth and slow release to the detent; wait for hissing to stop before pressing/turning it off, and secure it after checking. Repeat the pre-operation checklist. Complete only with actual pressure-test, riding, oil/debris, generator, repaired-part fit, tank-cleaning, chassis and all-joint records accepted. Missing required work remains pending.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.
